text_summary.body: Take from the exiles Heldai, Tobijah and Jedaiah, who have come from Babylon, and go to the house of Josiah son of Zephaniah; take silver and gold, make crowns and set them on the head of Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest. Say: the man whose name is the Branch will branch out and build the LORD's temple; he will bear royal honour and rule on his throne; a priest will be on his throne, and the counsel of peace will be between them both. The crowns will be a memorial in the temple; those far off will come and build.

setting.period: c. 519–516 BC (undated; between the visions of 519 and the oracle of Darius year 4)
setting.body: Gifts from exiles arriving from Babylon during the rebuilding. Mitchell notes that no descendant of David ruled again and the high priest later became head of the community.

constraints.subject: evt_01M4VN8BQJZ4XFNAWV5KE3VYHF
constraints.textual_assertion: The LORD's word came to me (following the night visions)
assumptions: Undated in the text; placed after the visions by narrative order only. Zech 7:1 (Darius year 4) follows.

constraints.subject: evt_01M4VN8BQJZ4XFNAWV5KE3VYHF
constraints.textual_assertion: He shall build the temple of the LORD
assumptions: The oracle speaks of the temple as still to be built.

locations.role: Crowning and memorial in the temple

terminology.gloss: Royal crowns, not the high priest's turban (Keil); the plural is variously explained (Keil: perhaps a silver and a gold one).

competing_reconstructions.label: Joshua crowned as a type of the priest-king Messiah
competing_reconstructions.summary: The words are addressed to Joshua alone; Zerubbabel must not be inserted.

competing_reconstructions.label: Zerubbabel originally crowned; the name changed to Joshua by a later scribe
competing_reconstructions.summary: Crowning Joshua would contradict Zechariah's own teaching that Zerubbabel would build the temple.

commentary.paraphrase: Guzik calls crowning a high priest unthinkable except as prophecy of the King-Priest Jesus and rejects emending the text to Zerubbabel.

open_questions: The identity and later history of Heldai, Tobijah, Jedaiah and Josiah son of Zephaniah are not researched.
